Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.14.3.
2. Create a new world or load an existing world from any gamemode.
3. Place an item on an anvil.
4. Rename the item with any string consisting of exactly 18 characters.
5. Attempt to delete all text in the anvil's rename field using the shift command delete.
6. Observe that the game crashes, displaying "saving world".
Observed Behavior: The issue occurs in Minecraft version 1.14.3 when players attempt to delete an 18-character string from an anvil using the Shift + Delete command. Upon executing this command, the game crashes while displaying a "saving world" message. The crash report indicates a java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, specifically stating that the string index is out of range. The stack trace reveals that the error arises from the substring method in the Java String class, which is called during the rendering of the anvil interface. The crash occurs on the client thread, and the error is associated with the rendering of buttons and text fields in the game's user interface. The affected world is set in the Overworld dimension, with two players present in the multiplayer environment. The game mode is set to survival, and the server is identified as a non-integrated vanilla server. The crash report provides details about the mouse location and screen size at the time of the crash, as well as information about the chunk cache and level spawn location. The issue persists across different worlds and game modes, making it a critical bug that affects gameplay when using the anvil interface.
Expected Behavior: When the player uses the Shift + Delete command to remove an 18-character string in the anvil's text input, the game should successfully delete the text without crashing. The interface should remain responsive, allowing the player to continue editing or renaming the item as intended. This expected behavior should occur consistently in Minecraft version 1.14.3, ensuring a smooth user experience without any errors or interruptions.
